Customer prioritizes multilingual support (EN, ES, FR), medical-domain fidelity for annotations, and strict latency SLOs for user-facing features. transcript:
Header:
- Date/Time: 2025-10-03 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Head of ML, Arbor AI), Ethan Cole (CTO), Marisol Vega (Eng Manager)

Auto-generated summary: (may be imperfect) POC scope, models, perf plan, security ask.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you blocking the hour. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account, with Liam our SE.
00:14 Speaker 2 (Liam): Hi all, Liam here. Quick agenda: confirm POC goals, workload shape, shortlist a few open models, and map out benchmarks and timeline.
00:27 Speaker 3 (Priya): Thanks, Maya. We're excited. Quick context: Arbor AI builds clinical summarization and triage for telehealth. Need models that handle English and Spanish primarily, maybe French for a small userbase. Also domain fidelity for medical notes — hallucination tolerance is low.
00:48 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great context. Priya, can you share the main success criteria for the POC? Like accuracy thresholds, latency, cost, and timeline?
01:02 Speaker 3 (Priya): Sure. For accuracy we want entity extraction + summary fidelity > our current baseline (proprietary rule-based) by measurable delta — target roughly 8-10% F1 improvement on our eval set. Latency: user-facing calls need p95 under 700ms ideally, p99 under 1.5s. Cost: we'd like to keep per-call token cost below our internal threshold, but willing to trade for accuracy. Timeline: 6-week pilot, deliverables at week 2 (baseline), week 4 (benchmark results), week 6 (recommendation).
01:38 Speaker 4 (Ethan): On concurrency, peak traffic is around 80 QPS currently for the triage endpoint, but bursty — up to 200 QPS for short periods. For the POC, we expect lower load but need to validate autoscaling behavior.
01:55 Speaker 2 (Liam): Good, that gives us shape. For the POC we'll size for ~50-100 QPS steady with headroom for bursts to 200. We'll recommend test scenarios for steady and burst.
02:12 Speaker 5 (Marisol): One ask — all data used in benchmarks must stay within our VPC or at least be hashed/anonymized. We'll share samples but need data handling details.
02:25 Speaker 1 (Maya): Understood. We'll provide the data-in-transit and at-rest encryption details and can run the pilot in Redwood Dedicated or Private if needed.
02:36 Speaker 3 (Priya): How about model selection? We're leaning to open models. Which ones should we try given multilingual and medical domain needs?
02:50 Speaker 2 (Liam): Our recommended shortlist for open models for this use case: Llama2-13B-instruct (quantized), Mistral-Instruct 7B/8B variants, Falcon-40B-instruct (if memory/perf allows), and for a cheaper baseline Mistral-7B or LLAMA3-7B-like variants; also consider Med-specific fine-tuned checkpoints if you have labelled data.
03:22 Speaker 3 (Priya): A couple names there — is Llama2 still a solid option for medical text? And you mentioned LLAMA3 — that's not public yet right?
03:33 Speaker 2 (Liam): Right, Llama2-13B has been a good balance of accuracy vs cost when quantized to 4-bit; it'll do fairly well on general summarization. Llama3 reference was generic — we meant newer community models that approximate that size; we can be explicit in the doc. Falcon-40B is high quality but needs heavier infra and may blow cost targets unless carefully quantized.
03:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): Also raising the point that redwood has routing and fallback — so for the POC you could route critical requests to a higher-quality model and cheaper ones to a lower tier to save cost while meeting SLOs.
04:14 Speaker 4 (Ethan): How realistic is that routing? We can't add too much complexity to our infra.
04:23 Speaker 2 (Liam): We can expose it as a policy in the request layer; Redwood Console can route by latency tolerance, user tier, or confidence threshold. Implementation is minimal from your side — mostly config.
04:35 Speaker 3 (Priya): On multilingual: do these open models have strong Spanish performance out of the box?
04:42 Speaker 2 (Liam): Varies. Llama2-13B works but has weaker Spanish than English. Mistral-based models tend to be very competitive and some community variants are trained with stronger multilingual corpora. We should test both — we'll include Spanish test set in the benchmark.
05:01 Speaker 5 (Marisol): And domain adaptation — we don't have time to fine-tune extensively, but could do LoRA or lightweight fine-tuning?
05:10 Speaker 2 (Liam): LoRA or instruction-tuning with adapters is a good middle ground. For POC we can try prompt engineering and small LoRA on a few hundred examples to see lift. If you want to avoid model-touch, we can use few-shot priming with examples and retrieval augmentation.
05:27 Speaker 3 (Priya): Retrieval augmentation — privacy concerns. Can we host the vector store in our VPC?
05:33 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, with Redwood Private or Dedicated we can have customer-managed vector store or E2E encryption. We'll include architecture options in the doc.
05:44 Speaker 2 (Liam): Moving to benchmarks: we'll measure accuracy (F1 for entity extraction, Rouge/BLEU-ish for summary, but we'll propose more tailored metrics), latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens-per-call cost, and resilience under load (tail latencies during bursts). We'll instrument KV cache hit rates and batching impact.
06:09 Speaker 4 (Ethan): For load tests, we also want to validate cold-start on autoscaling and model swap fallbacks.
06:17 Speaker 2 (Liam): Noted — we will include cold-start scenarios. We'll also include quantization profiles (int8/4-bit where supported) and measure quality delta.
06:28 Speaker 3 (Priya): What about deterministic behavior and explainability — we need to log model outputs and confidence scores for audit.
06:36 Speaker 1 (Maya): Redwood provides audit logs and token-level tracing in the Console. We'll share retention options and how logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
06:48 Speaker 5 (Marisol): Great. On the timeline: you said 6 weeks. Can you outline week-by-week deliverables?
06:56 Speaker 2 (Liam): Week 0: Kickoff and dataset handoff. Week 1-2: Baseline runs on current heuristics + initial model shortlist (Llama2-13B, Mistral-Instruct, Falcon-40B minimal). Week 3-4: More intensive benchmarks, quantized variants, LoRA tests. Week 5: Consolidate results, cost analysis. Week 6: Final recommendations and next steps (Dedicated pilot vs hosted).
07:21 Speaker 3 (Priya): Sounds good. For the POC environment, would you recommend Redwood Hosted API or Dedicated?
07:29 Speaker 1 (Maya): For initial speed to value, Hosted is fastest. For strict data controls and VPC egress, Dedicated or Private is recommended. Since you mentioned privacy and vector store in VPC, Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pool) is likely the right path for pilot if you want isolation and predictable perf.
07:46 Speaker 4 (Ethan): What's the uplift in cost for Dedicated vs Hosted?
07:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): It depends on commit and pool size. We'll send a pricing matrix. Generally Dedicated increases fixed cost but reduces per-token variability and gives isolation. We'll include examples in the pricing sheet.
08:05 Speaker 2 (Liam): Back to models — suggested concrete shortlist for benchmark phase: 1) Llama2-13B-instruct (4-bit quantized), 2) Mistral-Instruct-7B (and 8B if available), 3) Falcon-40B-instruct (baseline high-quality), 4) Mistral-7B or smaller community distill for cost baseline. We'll also include a retrieval-augmented variant of the best candidate.
08:35 Speaker 3 (Priya): Any concerns on hallucination for Llama2 vs Mistral?
08:40 Speaker 2 (Liam): Hallucination profiles differ — Falcon and Mistral variants often produce more factually dense outputs with proper prompts and retrieval. Llama2 can be tuned with LoRA or prompting. We'll capture hallucination rate in the evals using your annotated set.
08:55 Speaker 5 (Marisol): We have about 600 annotated records—some with Spanish. We'll give a 100-sample eval holdout for the POC.
09:02 Speaker 3 (Priya): We're sending a mixture of notes, SOAP formatted, and short patient messages. Please confirm formatting expectations.
09:10 Speaker 2 (Liam): We'll paste a schema and upload options. We can accept JSONL with fields: id, text, language, label. We'll also accept CSV if easier.
09:21 Speaker 1 (Maya): Security requests — Priya mentioned SOC2; we'll attach our SOC2 and ISO docs, and an FAQ about data residency.
09:32 Speaker 4 (Ethan): One more on benchmarking: how do you measure cost per call — tokens or compute?
09:37 Speaker 2 (Liam): We model cost as a function of tokens and GPU runtime; we report token counts, GPU-seconds and an estimated $/call under Hosted vs Dedicated assumptions. For Dedicated we can show marginal per-call costs at commit tiers.
09:52 Speaker 3 (Priya): For the POC success metric, can we agree on two primary: 1) accuracy lift over baseline (target 8-10% F1), 2) p95 latency under 700ms in steady-state at 50-100 QPS?
10:03 Speaker 1 (Maya): That sounds reasonable. We'll include a third softer metric around cost (target per-call budget).
10:12 Speaker 5 (Marisol): Are there recommended prompt templates or filters for medical extraction?
10:18 Speaker 2 (Liam): Yes, we'll share prompt templates and an eval harness. We also recommend retrieval augmentation for context windows and small LoRA for named entity fidelity.
10:30 Speaker 3 (Priya): One last question: what's your rollback/fallback if quality regresses in production?
10:36 Speaker 1 (Maya): Redwood supports automatic fallback policies and can route to a previous verified model; we also support canary rollouts and automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to evals. We'll show examples in the doc.
10:51 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Ok good. Next steps recap?
10:55 Speaker 1 (Maya): Recap — Maya sends pricing + SLOs + SOC2 link; Liam sends benchmark plan and templates; Priya uploads sample evals; schedule technical deep dive for next week.
11:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): Thanks, everyone. This is helpful.
11:15 Speaker 2 (Liam): Thanks, we'll follow up with the doc and calendar invite.
11:20 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: some product names transcribed slightly off (e.g., Redwood Dedicate vs Dedicated), and a few acronyms garbled. Intent preserved.
